messages.content:
You write realistic support tickets that clinic staff send to the support team of a fictional practice-management product. It has no brand name: never name it, and never name a real company, product or person. Write one ticket per brief. A ticket is a single email-style message with a subject and a body, in the requester's own voice, about the brief's topic, matching its situation, tone and level of detail:
- brief: one or two sentences
- moderate: three to five sentences
- detailed: a short paragraph or two with specifics, such as what they clicked, what they saw and what they already tried
Describe the problem the way a busy clinic employee would, not in the topic's words. Never mention the brief, topics, areas or situations. Never include a patient's real details: say 'a patient' or use made-up initials.

Reply with only a JSON object and no other text.
Output: ticket_texts.
The JSON object must match this JSON schema:

Thank you."}, {"id": "gen-082", "subject": "Assistance Needed with Pharmacy Substitution Messaging and Out-of-Stock Protocols", "body": "Hello Support, our clinical team is encountering several out-of-stock notices from local pharmacies and we need guidance on how to properly execute therapeutic alternative switches within the software. Specifically, when we receive a pharmacy notification stating a drug is unavailable, we attempt to navigate to the prescribing module to select an alternative agent, but the messaging workflow for substitution does not seem to transmit our instructions correctly back to the pharmacist. We have tried cancelling and re-issuing the electronic order using standard dropdowns, yet the pharmacy continues to report receiving ambiguous status codes. Could you please provide detailed instructions or documentation on the correct sequence for handling these substitution alerts so our providers can clear their pending queues efficiently?"}, {"id": "gen-083", "subject": "Fixing misapplied insurance payments on multiple invoice lines", "body": "I am so tired of fighting with this billing module every time a remittance comes in. When I post payments across multiple lines for a single claim, the system keeps shifting the amounts to random line items instead of matching what is on the actual remittance advice. I tried backing out the batch and re-entering it twice, but it keeps scrambling everything. Please tell me how to fix this before my month-end close is completely ruined."}, {"id": "gen-084", "subject": "Prescription sent wrong medication!", "body": "A script just went out with the completely wrong drug because my saved list got wiped out after the last patch. Fix this immediately."}, {"id": "gen-085", "subject": "Cannot find local pharmacies in directory or add custom ones", "body": "I've been trying to update a patient's preferred location because their usual spot shut down last week, but the search tool keeps returning zero results for the zip code. When I try to manually type in a custom pharmacy entry to bypass the lookup, the save button remains grayed out. This is holding up our outbound orders and wasting a lot of time."}, {"id": "gen-086", "subject": "Critical workflow breakdown regarding medication substitution alerts and out-of-stock messages", "body": "Our providers are completely blocked by how the system handles pharmacy alerts for unavailable medications. When an out-of-stock notification arrives in our inbox, clicking the substitution link often leads to a blank screen or a generic error code instead of opening the alternative drug menu. We have tried clearing our browser cache, restarting workstations, and navigating through the main chart instead of the task center, but nothing works. This is causing massive delays in getting maintenance medications to our patients, and we urgently need someone to look into why these messaging pathways are failing."}, {"id": "gen-087", "subject": "Restoration of Missing Personal Medication Favorites Following System Update", "body": "Dear Support Team, following the recent software deployment implemented over the weekend, my personal preference list of frequently prescribed medications and associated sigs has completely disappeared from my profile. I have attempted to recreate a few entries by searching the master formulary manually, but this significantly impedes my charting efficiency during patient encounters. Could you please investigate our practice database backups and restore my custom medication favorites as soon as possible? Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter."}, {"id": "gen-088", "subject": "Pharmacy directory search failure and custom entry options", "body": "The directory search is not finding newly opened local pharmacies. How do we manually add a custom pharmacy entry so we can send our electronic prescriptions without further delay?"}, {"id": "gen-089", "subject": "Lost all my medication favorites again", "body": "Every time there's an update, all my custom medication favorites vanish from my profile. It takes forever to rebuild them manually while patients are waiting. Can you please restore my list and tell me why this keeps happening?"}, {"id": "gen-090", "subject": "Errors when trying to upload scanned paper lab reports to patient charts", "body": "I am at my wit's end trying to attach outside paper lab reports and imaging PDFs into patient records today. Every single time I try to upload a scanned document that is slightly larger than normal, the system spins for five minutes and then throws a generic upload failed error without any explanation. I have tried reducing the file size, scanning at a lower DPI, and renaming the files to simple text, but nothing lets me attach these records. We are drowning in paper because the document intake tool is completely unusable right now, and I need a fix immediately."}]}
